candidates.label: Roman Forum, Philippi
candidates.support: The Greek Ministry of Culture and Sports describes the Roman forum as the administrative centre of the city, a complex of public buildings around a central square. No dataset entry gives a coordinate for the forum distinct from the wider archaeological site, so this point, Philippi's own representative point, marks the general area of the city center where the forum stood rather than the forum's exact footprint.

summary.text: The marketplace (forum) of Philippi was the city's administrative and commercial center, a paved square ringed by public buildings and temples. According to Acts, after Paul drove a spirit of divination out of a slave girl, her owners seized Paul and his companion Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the city's rulers, who had them beaten and imprisoned.

history.text: Acts records that the owners of a slave girl whose fortune-telling had profited them, seeing their hope of gain gone after Paul freed her from a "spirit of divination," dragged Paul and Silas into the marketplace before the rulers, accusing them of disturbing the city and advocating customs unlawful for Romans; the crowd and magistrates had them beaten with rods and thrown into prison.

The Greek Ministry of Culture and Sports describes the visible Roman forum as a unified complex of public buildings around a central square, with two monumental temples at its northeast and northwest corners, and notes that a large paved road just north of the forum has been identified as the Via Egnatia, the Roman road on which Philippi stood.

scripture.textWEB: But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.
